# B2 Reference Architectures for Robotics: full text

> Generated by tools/generate_catalog.py from the pages listed below; links are relative to the repository root. Product behavior is authoritative at https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning.

<!-- source: docs/robotics.md -->

# Robotics on Backblaze B2 (agent-readable)

Catalog updated: 2026-11-16. Current product behavior is authoritative in the [Backblaze B2 documentation](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage).

## Workload
Robotics teams produce data at every stage. Fleets record rosbag2/MCAP logs sized by topic rates and recording duration, teleoperation produces demonstration datasets, simulation produces rollout sweeps, mobile robots produce LiDAR mapping sessions, and training produces multi-GB policy checkpoints. Most of it is written once, read many times by replay tools, dataloaders and trainers, and rarely deleted.

## Where does B2 fit?
B2 is the S3-compatible system of record behind that work: raw log lakes, versioned dataset releases, rollout sinks, checkpoint and policy release prefixes, and Object Lock evidence. Choose the connection method documented for each tool:

- **Built-in Backblaze B2 option:** MLflow (`b2://` artifact URI) and rclone (B2 backend).
- **S3 custom endpoint:** Ray Train, W&B, ClearML, Foxglove self-managed Primary Site (`s3_compatible`), DuckDB, DVC, Daft, Isaac Sim asset region profiles. Set the endpoint to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the bucket region.
- **fsspec / s3fs:** Zarr replay buffers through `s3fs.S3FileSystem(endpoint_url=...)`.
- **Presigned URLs:** browser viewers (the Foxglove app with remote files, the Rerun Web Viewer) take presigned GETs; robots upload with presigned PUTs.
- **S3 sync tool:** rosbag2, LeRobot, MuJoCo Playground, KISS-ICP and Open3D write local files; an offload agent, rclone or s5cmd moves closed files to and from B2. Backblaze samples ([Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload), [LeRobot B2 Streaming](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lerobot-b2-streaming), [MuJoCo Rollout Dataset](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/mujoco-rollout-dataset), [KISS-ICP LiDAR Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/kiss-icp-lidar-archive), [Open3D Point Cloud Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/open3d-point-cloud-pipeline)) show the same flows written directly against the S3 API.

## Can I use B2 with ROS 2 rosbag2?
Yes. Record split MCAP files, presigned-PUT each closed split to `bags/<robot>/<session>/`, retain the local copy until the offload service verifies the uploaded version's size and full-file SHA-256. See [robot-log-offload](architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md).

## Can I open B2 logs in Foxglove or Rerun?
Yes, with presigned GET URLs and bucket CORS rules for the viewer origin; Foxglove also requires range requests and no redirects. A self-managed Foxglove Primary Site uses B2 as its `s3_compatible` inbox and lake; configure a B2 Event Notification adapter that forwards object-created events to it. See [fleet-search-replay](architectures/fleet-search-replay/architecture.md).

## Can I train from B2?
Yes. Ray Train, MLflow, W&B and ClearML document Backblaze B2 by name; trainers stream LeRobot v3 episodes or WebDataset shards with ranged GETs. See [teleop-imitation-datasets](architectures/teleop-imitation-datasets/architecture.md) and [policy-training-registry](architectures/policy-training-registry/architecture.md).

## B2 capabilities that apply
S3-compatible API; range GET; presigned GET, PUT and upload-part URLs; bucket CORS rules; multipart upload; application keys restricted to one bucket and one name prefix with listed capabilities; server-side copy (CopyObject, UploadPartCopy); batch DeleteObjects (without a VersionId it only hides files; purge with a lifecycle rule or delete by VersionId); lifecycle rules (hide, then delete, by age and prefix); Event Notifications (enabled by Backblaze Support on request; webhook, signed, at-least-once); Object Lock (governance or compliance, retention and legal hold); included egress (see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)).

## Reference architectures
- [robot-log-offload](architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md): buckets `<org>-robot-logs` (`bags/`, `catalog/`, `events/`) and `<org>-robot-evidence` (Object Lock, `evidence/<incident_id>/`).
- [fleet-search-replay](architectures/fleet-search-replay/architecture.md): DuckDB over `catalog/`, presigned GETs to Foxglove and Rerun, and presigned downloads for local `ros2 bag play`.
- [teleop-imitation-datasets](architectures/teleop-imitation-datasets/architecture.md): drafts under `drafts/<name>/`, LeRobot v3 or Zarr releases under `datasets/<name>/<version>/`, curated with Daft, optionally tracked with DVC, streamed with ranged GETs.
- [sim-rollout-datasets](architectures/sim-rollout-datasets/architecture.md): assets under `sim-assets/`, episodes under `rollouts/<env>/<policy>/<run_id>/`, promotion by server-side copy.
- [policy-training-registry](architectures/policy-training-registry/architecture.md): `checkpoints/<run_id>/`, `eval/`, and an Object Lock release bucket `models/<policy>/<version>/`.
- [mapping-session-archive](architectures/mapping-session-archive/architecture.md): `scans/`, `maps/`, `trajectories/`, `jobs/`, and approved `sitemaps/<site>/<version>/`.

## When Overdrive may apply
Sustained high-throughput reads where storage, not compute, is the bottleneck: many training nodes streaming one dataset version for long periods, or bulk re-processing of a large log lake. Interactive replay and fleet uploads (bounded by site uplinks) do not need it. Confirm with [Backblaze](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive). For repeated epochs or replays of the same immutable data, a local NVMe cache is usually the first step.

## Where B2 does not fit
- The live ROS graph, DDS transport and real-time robot state.
- Partially written bags, HDF5 files and episodes; upload only closed files.
- Upload queues, tracking-server databases, search indexes, leaderboards and metrics time series.
- Simulator and GPU state, Ray object-store memory, training rendezvous.
- POSIX in-place edits and live USD collaboration.
- Fleet or customer delivery via Cloud Replication; replication is bucket-to-bucket DR.

## Links
[README](README.md) - [Architecture index](docs/architecture-index.md) - [Related B2 samples](docs/related-b2-samples.md) - [Configuration examples](examples/README.md) - [B2 docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) - [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) - [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api) - [Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications) - [Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)

<!-- source: architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md -->

# Offload robot logs from the fleet into a raw log lake

## Workload

Robots record ROS 2 topics with `ros2 bag record` into split rosbag2 files (MCAP by default in current ROS 2 distributions), capped by duration or size. Size the local buffer from recording rate, offline duration, and the site offload window. Engineers need every session to land in durable storage with enough metadata to find it later, and they need incident windows preserved unchanged for safety review.

B2 is the raw log lake and the evidence store. The robot keeps only a bounded buffer and an upload queue; it never holds a B2 application key.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  REC[ros2 bag record<br/>closed MCAP splits] --> BUF[(On-robot buffer<br/>+ upload queue)]
  BUF -->|request URL| SIGN[Site offload service<br/>holds offload-signer key]
  SIGN -->|presigned PUT or<br/>upload-part URLs| BUF
  BUF -->|PUT split| LOGS[(B2 log bucket<br/>bags/robot/session/)]
  SIGN -->|GET uploaded version<br/>and verify SHA-256| LOGS
  SIGN -->|verified receipt: delete local| BUF
  DOCK[Depot / dock / drive swap] -->|rclone b2 backend| LOGS
  LOGS -->|inline, or Event Notification| DESC[Describe + catalog job]
  DESC -->|metadata.json, Parquet| CAT[(B2 log bucket<br/>catalog/)]
  EDGE[Edge perception<br/>flagged frames] -->|presigned PUT| EVT[(B2 log bucket<br/>events/robot/)]
  LOGS -->|server-side copy| EVID[(B2 evidence bucket<br/>Object Lock<br/>evidence/incident/)]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as Robot agent
  participant S as Site offload service
  participant B as B2 (S3 API)
  R->>S: split closed (robot, session, name, size, sha256)
  alt size <= 5 GB
    S-->>R: presigned PUT (short TTL)
    R->>B: PUT object
    B-->>R: Object version ID
    R->>S: Upload completed (key, version ID)
  else size > 5 GB
    S->>B: CreateMultipartUpload
    S-->>R: presigned UploadPart URLs
    R->>B: PUT parts
    R->>S: part ETags
    S->>B: CompleteMultipartUpload
    B-->>S: Object version ID
  end
  S->>B: GET object with VersionId
  B-->>S: Stored bytes
  S->>S: Compare byte count and full-file SHA-256
  S-->>R: Verified (key, version ID, size, SHA-256)
  R->>R: delete local split
```

Object names are derived from robot, session, and split name. A retry can create a new B2 version; the `bags/` lifecycle rule purges superseded versions after its retention window. The offload service reads the exact uploaded version and compares its byte count and full-file SHA-256 with the closed split. It returns a receipt containing the key, version ID, size, and verified digest before the robot removes its local copy. Reuse a receipt only when the source digest and stored version match; size alone is insufficient. A single presigned PUT is limited to 5 GB, so larger splits use presigned upload-part URLs.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw splits | `<org>-robot-logs/bags/<robot>/<session>/` | Hide after the retention window, delete hidden versions after a grace period ([lifecycle-log-lake.json](examples/lifecycle-log-lake.json)) | No | Every recorded split, as written by rosbag2, plus its `metadata.yaml` |
| Session catalog | `<org>-robot-logs/catalog/` | Keep current; hidden versions purge after the grace period | No | Per-session `metadata.json` and the rolled Parquet catalog |
| Edge events | `<org>-robot-logs/events/<robot>/` | Shorter retention than raw splits | No | Flagged frames and prediction JSON used as triage signals |
| Evidence | `<org>-robot-evidence/evidence/<incident_id>/` | Lifecycle does not remove versions under retention or legal hold | Yes, governance by default ([object-lock-evidence.json](examples/object-lock-evidence.json)) | Server-side copies of incident windows plus a SHA-256 manifest |

Evidence is a separate bucket because Object Lock, default retention and lifecycle are bucket-level controls; keeping it apart stops a raw-log retention change from touching evidence. The bucket names are placeholders: B2 bucket names are globally unique.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Live ROS graph and topic transport | DDS on the robot | Real-time messaging, not objects |
| Partially written splits and the on-robot buffer | Robot SSD | A split becomes an object only once it is closed |
| Upload queue and dedupe state | Robot-local database or file | Must survive reboots and link loss without a network round trip |
| Incident case management | Ticketing or safety system | Transactional records; it links to evidence keys |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | All reads and writes; endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from the bucket region |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Presigned PUT and presigned UploadPart for robot uploads |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Splits over 5 GB and rclone large-file transfers |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | One bucket and one prefix per key; robots get URLs, not keys |
| Event Notifications | Optional | `b2:ObjectCreated:*` on `bags/` triggers describe; Backblaze Support must enable the feature ([event-notifications.json](examples/event-notifications.json)) |
| Object versions and lifecycle | Yes | Hide then delete raw splits and edge events by age |
| Object Lock | Yes | Evidence bucket only; retention or legal hold per incident |
| Server-side copy | Yes | CopyObject, or UploadPartCopy for objects over 5 GB, into the evidence bucket |
| SSE-B2 / SSE-C | Not required | Enable SSE-B2 default encryption if policy requires encryption at rest beyond B2 defaults |
| Cloud Replication | Not used | Bucket-to-bucket DR only; see the ordering caveat in [examples](examples/README.md#object-lock-and-replication) |
| CORS | Not used here | Only needed for browser viewers, covered in [fleet-search-replay](architectures/fleet-search-replay/architecture.md) |
| Overdrive | Not needed | Upload rate is bounded by site uplinks; Standard B2 is the default |

## Integration configuration

### ROS 2 rosbag2

rosbag2 writes bag files to local disk; [split them by size or duration](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2#splitting-files-during-recording) (`ros2 bag record -s mcap -d <seconds>`) so each split closes and uploads independently. The [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload) sample demonstrates presigned-PUT offload, session metadata, Parquet cataloging, and presigned replay. Apply the version-specific checksum and acknowledgment requirements in the data flow above to local cleanup.

- Endpoint: derive `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from `B2_REGION`; never hardcode it.
- Keys: the site service holds `offload-signer` (`listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` on `bags/`) and `catalog-writer` (on `catalog/`). See [scoped keys](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Use presigned upload-part URLs for splits over 5 GB, Event Notifications for the describe step, and a separate Object Lock bucket for evidence.

### rclone

The [rclone B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/) is a native B2 option for depots, docking stations and drive-swap ingest. Tune `--b2-chunk-size` and `--b2-upload-concurrency` for large splits. Give rclone its own key restricted to `bags/`. Use `rclone copy` from a staging directory populated only after the recorder closes each split; delete the local file after the offload service returns its checksum-verification receipt.

### Edge-triggered capture

The [Roboflow Inference Frame Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/roboflow-inference-frame-archive) sample shows the pattern for uploading only flagged frames, their prediction JSON, and Parquet roll-ups instead of continuous video. Here those objects go under `events/<robot>/` and serve as pointers into the raw splits.

## Security

- Robots hold no B2 keys. A compromised robot can write only the object names it was given URLs for, and only until those URLs expire.
- Keep presigned URL TTLs short and log every signing request with robot ID and key.
- The evidence writer is the only role with `writeFileRetentions` and `writeFileLegalHolds`; promotion across buckets uses a short-lived key covering both buckets (see [examples](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys)).
- Use governance-mode Object Lock by default. Compliance mode cannot be shortened or removed, even by the account owner.
- Record a SHA-256 manifest with each evidence copy so later reviewers can verify bytes independently of B2.
- Secrets go in a gitignored `0600` `.env` or a secret manager; never print or log keys.

## References

- [ROS 2 rosbag2](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2)
- [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload architecture](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [rclone B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/fleet-search-replay/architecture.md -->

# Search, visualize and replay fleet sessions from the log lake

## Workload

Robotics engineers triage field issues, review autonomy behavior and pull sessions for labeling. They need to find the right ten minutes across thousands of robot-days, open it in a viewer, and replay it locally, without bulk-downloading terabytes. This architecture reads the log lake that [robot-log-offload](architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md) writes.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CAT[(B2 log bucket<br/>catalog/ Parquet)] -->|DuckDB httpfs<br/>range reads| Q[Search service / notebook]
  Q -->|selected splits| SIGN[Signing service<br/>replay-signer + rrd-signer keys]
  SIGN -->|presigned GET| FOX[Foxglove app<br/>browser]
  SIGN -->|presigned GET| RR[Rerun Web Viewer]
  SIGN -->|presigned GET manifest| PLAY[ros2 bag play<br/>engineer workstation]
  CONV[Conversion job<br/>Rerun SDK, rrd-writer key] -->|PUT .rrd| BAGS
  FOX -->|HTTP Range + CORS| BAGS[(B2 log bucket<br/>bags/ and rrd/)]
  RR -->|HTTP + CORS| BAGS
  PLAY -->|presigned GET download,<br/>then local playback| BAGS
  subgraph Optional self-managed indexing
    INBOX[(B2 inbox bucket)] -->|object-created event| PS[Foxglove Primary Site<br/>s3_compatible]
    PS --> LAKE[(B2 lake bucket)]
    PS -->|stream| FOX
  end
```

1. `catalog/` holds one Parquet row per session or split: robot, time range, topics, ROS distribution and tags.
2. DuckDB queries the catalog in place with range reads and returns object keys.
3. A signing service mints short-lived presigned GETs for those keys.
4. The Foxglove app opens each MCAP over HTTP range requests; the Rerun Web Viewer loads `.rrd` recordings from presigned URLs; for `ros2 bag play`, the workstation downloads the splits from a presigned GET manifest and plays them locally, as in the Rosbag2 Cloud Offload sample.
5. Optionally, a self-managed Foxglove Primary Site ingests from a B2 inbox bucket into an indexed B2 lake bucket and streams sessions to the Foxglove app.

`.rrd` files are optional and are not written by robot-log-offload. A conversion job you own reads selected sessions, logs the topics you want with the Rerun SDK, saves an `.rrd`, and writes it under `rrd/<robot>/<session>/` with the `rrd-writer` key. Skip the `rrd/` zone if you do not use Rerun.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session catalog | `<org>-robot-logs/catalog/` | Owned by [robot-log-offload](architectures/robot-log-offload/architecture.md) | No | Parquet index queried in place |
| Raw splits | `<org>-robot-logs/bags/<robot>/<session>/` | Owned by robot-log-offload | No | MCAP read by range requests |
| Rerun recordings | `<org>-robot-logs/rrd/<robot>/<session>/` | Same windows as raw splits ([lifecycle-log-lake.json](examples/lifecycle-log-lake.json)) | No | `.rrd` files written by the conversion job for the Rerun Web Viewer |
| Primary Site inbox (optional) | `<org>-foxglove-inbox/` | Short; Primary Site moves data to the lake | No | Upload target that triggers indexing |
| Primary Site lake (optional) | `<org>-foxglove-lake/` | Managed by Primary Site | No | Indexed recordings served to Foxglove |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Live search and tag index | Postgres, ClickHouse, or the Primary Site index database | Low-latency queries and updates |
| Viewer UI state and user auth | Foxglove, Rerun, or your identity provider | Per-user sessions |
| Hot replay cache | Local NVMe on workstations or replay hosts | Repeated reads of the same session |
| Live robot streams | Foxglove bridge / ROS graph | Real-time data, not archived objects |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | DuckDB, signing service, Primary Site |
| Range GET | Yes | DuckDB Parquet reads, Foxglove MCAP seeks; `ros2 bag play` downloads splits whole |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | GET only, short TTL |
| Bucket CORS | Yes | `s3_get` and `s3_head` for viewer origins ([cors-viewers.json](examples/cors-viewers.json)) |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Read-only, restricted to `bags/`, `rrd/` or `catalog/` (one prefix per key); `rrd-writer` for the conversion job |
| Included egress | Yes | Repeated range reads by viewers and replay; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for terms |
| Event Notifications | Only with Primary Site | Inbox object-created events; Backblaze Support must enable the feature |
| Object Lock, replication | Not used | Evidence locking lives in robot-log-offload |
| Overdrive | Rarely | Interactive reads are latency-bound; consider it only for sustained bulk re-processing of the lake |
| Local cache | Yes | NVMe cache for sessions replayed repeatedly |

## Integration configuration

### DuckDB (httpfs)

Documented S3 secret with a custom endpoint:

```sql
CREATE SECRET b2 (
  TYPE s3,
  KEY_ID '<from env>', SECRET '<from env>',
  ENDPOINT 's3.<region>.backblazeb2.com',
  REGION '<region>',
  URL_STYLE 'path'
);
SELECT robot, session, start_time FROM read_parquet('s3://<org>-robot-logs/catalog/*.parquet')
WHERE list_contains(topics, '/estop');
```

Use a read-only key restricted to `catalog/`. Load secrets from the environment, never from a committed file. The [DuckDB Query In Place](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/duckdb-query-in-place) sample shows the same pattern against B2.

### Foxglove app (remote files)

Foxglove's [remote file docs](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/visualization/connecting/cloud-data) describe opening a file by URL. Requirements stated there: the server must support range requests, must not redirect (redirects break CORS), and must send CORS headers that allow the Foxglove origins and expose the headers it needs. Give Foxglove a presigned GET straight to the B2 object, and apply [cors-viewers.json](examples/cors-viewers.json) to the log bucket.

Foxglove's hosted bring-your-own-storage lists AWS, GCP and Azure; for B2, use presigned remote files or a self-managed Primary Site.

### Foxglove Primary Site (self-managed)

The [installation](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/primary-sites/installation) and [cloud credentials](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/primary-sites/configure-cloud-credentials) pages document `storageProvider: s3_compatible` and `S3_COMPATIBLE_SERVICE_URL`. Set it to `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` for both the inbox and lake buckets. Primary Site indexes the inbox from object-created notifications, delivered either by provider push or by a POST to the Primary Site `/site-bucket-notifications` endpoint. B2 Event Notifications are webhooks with B2-specific JSON (HMAC-signed, at-least-once), so configure them on the inbox bucket (Backblaze Support enables the feature for the account) and run a small adapter that verifies the B2 signature and POSTs each object-created event to `/site-bucket-notifications`. Make the adapter idempotent, since events can repeat. The [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) sample receives and forwards B2 events.

### Rerun Web Viewer

The [WebViewer API](https://ref.rerun.io/docs/js/0.37.0/web-viewer/classes/WebViewer.html) accepts an HTTP URL to an `.rrd` file. Serve it with a presigned GET and add the viewer origin to the CORS rules. For the native viewer, download the `.rrd` by presigned GET and open it locally.

### ros2 bag play

The Rosbag2 Cloud Offload sample generates a presigned GET manifest for a session's splits; the client downloads them and replays them locally with `ros2 bag play`. This is a sample pattern; rosbag2 itself does not read from S3 or HTTP.

## Security

- Viewers receive presigned GETs, never keys. Keep TTLs short; shared links are bearer credentials.
- Restrict CORS to the exact viewer origins and to `s3_get` and `s3_head`. Do not use `*`.
- The DuckDB and signing keys are read-only and restricted to the prefixes they need; only the conversion job's `rrd-writer` key can write `rrd/`.
- Primary Site keys (inbox read and delete, lake write) stay inside the Primary Site deployment.
- Log signing requests by user and session for audit.

## References

- [DuckDB S3 API support](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html)
- [Foxglove: open remote files](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/visualization/connecting/cloud-data)
- [Foxglove Primary Site installation](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/primary-sites/installation)
- [Foxglove Primary Site cloud credentials](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/primary-sites/configure-cloud-credentials)
- [Rerun WebViewer](https://ref.rerun.io/docs/js/0.37.0/web-viewer/classes/WebViewer.html)
- [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload)
- [B2 CORS rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cross-origin-resource-sharing-rules)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/teleop-imitation-datasets/architecture.md -->

# Record teleoperation demonstrations and stream imitation-learning datasets

## Workload

Imitation-learning teams collect demonstrations with leader-follower arms, VR or spacemouse teleoperation. Each episode is multi-camera video plus per-step state and action. Datasets reach TB scale and are read many times by many training workers. Released versions must stay byte-identical so a trained policy can be traced to exactly the data it saw.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  TELE[Teleop rig<br/>leader-follower / VR] --> WS[(Workstation buffer<br/>episode in progress)]
  WS -->|closed episode, S3 PUT| DRAFT[(B2 datasets bucket<br/>drafts/name/)]
  DRAFT -->|Daft / s3fs reads| CUR[Curation<br/>filter, relabel, QA]
  CUR -->|write new version| REL[(B2 datasets bucket<br/>datasets/name/version/)]
  REL -.->|optional dvc push| DVC[(B2 datasets bucket<br/>dvc/ content-addressed copy)]
  DVC -.->|pointers| GIT[DVC repo]
  REL -->|meta/episodes + ranged GETs| TRAIN[Training workers 1..N]
  REL -->|presigned GET MP4| REVIEW[Review UI]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Training worker k of N
  participant B as B2 (S3 API)
  W->>B: GET meta/info.json, meta/episodes/*.parquet
  W->>W: assign episodes k, k+N, ...
  loop each episode
    W->>B: ranged GET data Parquet footer
    W->>B: ranged GET row-group span for the episode
    W->>B: ranged GET MP4 byte window per camera
    W->>W: decode, slice frames, train step
  end
```

## Dataset layout

The LeRobot v3 format stores many episodes per shard and indexes them in `meta/episodes/`:

```
datasets/<name>/<version>/
  meta/info.json
  meta/stats.json
  meta/tasks.parquet
  meta/episodes/chunk-000/file-000.parquet   # per-episode frame and byte offsets
  data/chunk-000/file-000.parquet            # state and action rows
  videos/<camera>/chunk-000/file-000.mp4     # many episodes per shard
```

The `meta/episodes` rows carry frame ranges, shard indexes and per-video timestamps. These offsets let a reader plan ranged GETs for one episode without downloading whole shards. The sample stores one v3 tree per episode under `lerobot/episodes/ep_<n>/` to make deletes prefix-scoped; this architecture recommends one tree per released version instead, so a version is a single immutable prefix. Zarr replay buffers (diffusion policy, UMI) follow the same rule: `datasets/<name>/<version>/replay.zarr/`.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft episodes | `<org>-robot-datasets/drafts/<name>/` | Hide after the promotion window, then delete ([lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | No | Newly recorded episodes awaiting curation |
| Released versions | `<org>-robot-datasets/datasets/<name>/<version>/` | Never overwritten; no lifecycle rule | Optional, governance | Frozen dataset versions read by trainers |
| DVC remote (optional) | `<org>-robot-datasets/dvc/` | Content-addressed; keep | No | A second copy of each tracked file, stored by content hash |

Drafts live under a top-level `drafts/` prefix, not inside `datasets/`, so the recorder's prefix-restricted key cannot reach released versions even without Object Lock. If released versions must be locked, use a separate bucket with Object Lock enabled so draft deletes are unaffected.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| In-progress episode | Teleop workstation disk | Written frame by frame until closed |
| Task, label and curation queue | Application database | Transactional updates |
| DVC git repo | Git host | Holds pointers, not data |
| Hub mirror (optional) | Hugging Face Hub | Public or partner sharing; not the system of record here |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Recording writes, curation reads, training reads |
| Range GET | Yes | Parquet row groups and MP4 byte windows per episode |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | GET for review UIs |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Recorder restricted to `drafts/<name>/`; curation writes `datasets/<name>/`; trainers read-only on one version prefix ([keys](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys)) |
| Object Lock | Optional | Lock released versions in a dedicated bucket |
| Included egress | Yes | Multi-epoch streaming by many workers; see [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Multipart upload | As needed | Large MP4 shards from the SDK's upload path |
| Event Notifications | Not used | Curation is batch |
| Overdrive vs local cache | Consider | [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) for sustained multi-node streaming; local NVMe cache for repeated epochs of one version |

## Integration configuration

### Hugging Face LeRobot

LeRobot [records and loads v3 datasets](https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/lerobot-dataset-v3) from a local root. Call `dataset.finalize()`, then sync the dataset directory to `datasets/<name>/<version>/` with rclone or s5cmd; trainers sync a version back to their local root and load it with `LeRobotDataset(repo_id, root=...)`. To stream without a local copy, use the [LeRobot B2 Streaming](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lerobot-b2-streaming) sample: boto3 against `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` reads the data Parquet footer with a small ranged GET, fetches only the episode's row-group span, ranges the camera MP4 byte window, and decodes frames with torchcodec. It splits episodes across N workers.

### Daft

Daft documents `daft.datasets.lerobot.read` and S3 `IOConfig` with a custom endpoint:

```python
import daft
from daft.io import IOConfig, S3Config
io = IOConfig(s3=S3Config(endpoint_url=f"https://s3.{region}.backblazeb2.com",
                          key_id=key_id, access_key=app_key))
df = daft.datasets.lerobot.read("s3://<org>-robot-datasets/datasets/<name>/<version>", io_config=io)
```

Use it for lazy filtering, relabeling and quality checks; write results to a new version prefix.

### Zarr via s3fs

Zarr reaches B2 through fsspec. s3fs documents an `endpoint_url` argument: `s3fs.S3FileSystem(endpoint_url=f"https://s3.{region}.backblazeb2.com")` (`client_kwargs={"endpoint_url": ...}` also works). Write Zarr stores once and treat them as read-only after release. Zarr's in-place chunk updates are fine on a draft prefix but must not touch a released version.

### DVC

```bash
dvc remote add -d b2 s3://<org>-robot-datasets/dvc
dvc remote modify b2 endpointurl https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com
dvc remote modify --local b2 access_key_id "$B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID"
dvc remote modify --local b2 secret_access_key "$B2_APPLICATION_KEY"
```

`--local` keeps credentials in `.dvc/config.local`, which DVC does not commit.

`dvc push` uploads a second, content-addressed copy of each tracked file under `dvc/`; it does not point at the objects under `datasets/<name>/<version>/`. Either make DVC the system of record for released versions and skip the version-prefix copy, or skip DVC and pin versions by prefix. Storing both doubles the bytes. `dvc import-url` can reference external objects without copying them.

## Security

- The recording workstation writes only `drafts/<name>/` with the `recorder-writer` key; curation reads drafts and writes a new version prefix; trainers read one released prefix.
- Review UIs get short-lived presigned GETs.
- Teleop video can capture operators and bystanders. Record consent and redaction status in the dataset card.
- Never print keys; keep them in a gitignored `0600` `.env` or a secret manager.

## References

- [LeRobot](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot)
- [LeRobot B2 Streaming architecture](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lerobot-b2-streaming/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Daft LeRobot reader](https://docs.daft.ai/en/stable/datasets/lerobot/)
- [Daft IOConfig](https://docs.daft.ai/en/stable/api/config/)
- [Zarr](https://zarr.dev/) and [s3fs](https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)
- [DVC Amazon S3 remote](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3)
- [B2 S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)

<!-- source: architectures/sim-rollout-datasets/architecture.md -->

# Generate simulation rollouts and synthetic demonstrations at scale

## Workload

Simulation teams run policy sweeps, domain randomization and synthetic demonstration generation across many GPU workers. Each sweep loads the same robot and scene assets and produces many episodes: rendered video, per-step state, action and reward arrays, and a summary. Some runs are scratch; good ones become training data for behavioral cloning, offline RL or evaluation baselines. There is no shared filesystem across the farm.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ASSETS[(B2 sim bucket<br/>sim-assets/ USD, MJCF)] -->|S3 GET or asset profile| W1[Rollout worker 1]
  ASSETS --> WN[Rollout worker N]
  SCHED[Ray / cluster scheduler] --> W1
  SCHED --> WN
  W1 -->|completed episode only| RUN[(B2 sim bucket<br/>rollouts/env/policy/run_id/)]
  WN -->|completed episode only| RUN
  WN -->|closed HDF5| RCL[rclone sync] --> RUN
  RUN -->|presigned GET| EXP[Dataset explorer / review]
  RUN -->|server-side copy| DS[(B2 sim bucket<br/>datasets/name/version/)]
  RUN -->|delete by VersionId| GONE[Discarded run]
```

Each worker writes an episode only after it completes:

```
rollouts/<env>/<policy>/<run_id>/
  config.json                         # simulator, asset version, seed, policy checkpoint
  episode-<n>/video.mp4
  episode-<n>/states.npy
  episode-<n>/actions.npy
  episode-<n>/rewards.npy
  episode-<n>/summary.json
```

A retry writes the same keys again, so reruns stay inside their run prefix; on B2 each rewrite adds a new version and hides the previous one. Promotion copies a run into `datasets/<name>/<version>/` with server-side copy, so bytes do not leave B2. On B2, `DeleteObjects` without a `VersionId` only hides each file; the bytes stay stored. To remove them, list the prefix with `ListObjectVersions` and delete by `VersionId` (needs `deleteFiles`), or rely on the `daysFromHidingToDeleting` rule in [lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json), which purges hidden versions under `rollouts/` after a short grace period.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sim assets | `<org>-robot-sim/sim-assets/<asset>/<version>/` | Keep; new versions under new prefixes | No | Read-mostly USD, MJCF, meshes, textures |
| Scratch sweeps | `<org>-robot-sim/rollouts/scratch/` | Hide after a short window, then delete ([lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | No | Exploratory runs |
| Runs | `<org>-robot-sim/rollouts/<env>/<policy>/<run_id>/` | Keep until promoted or discarded; hidden versions purge after a grace period | No | Append-only episode outputs |
| Datasets | `<org>-robot-sim/datasets/<name>/<version>/` | Never overwritten | Optional, in a separate locked bucket | Promoted runs used for training |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Simulator and GPU state | Worker memory | Per-step state, not objects |
| Partially written HDF5 or episode buffers | Worker local disk | HDF5 updates in place; upload only closed files |
| Ray object store | Node memory | Inter-task data plane |
| Scheduler and job queue | Ray head / cluster scheduler | Transactional |
| USD live-edit sessions | Nucleus or a local workspace | Live collaborative editing is not object storage |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Asset reads and episode writes |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | GET for explorers and review |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Large videos and HDF5 files |
| Server-side copy | Yes | Promote a run to a dataset version |
| Version-aware deletes | Yes | `ListObjectVersions` plus `DeleteObjects` by `VersionId` for discarded runs |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire scratch sweeps (hide, then delete); purge hidden versions under `rollouts/` |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Workers write only `rollouts/`; assets read-only |
| Event Notifications | Not used | The scheduler already knows when a run finishes |
| Object Lock | Optional | Only for locked dataset releases in a separate bucket |
| Overdrive | Consider | When sustained sweep reads or writes saturate Standard throughput |
| Local cache | Yes | Cache sim assets on each node; they are reread every episode |

## Integration configuration

### MuJoCo Playground

MuJoCo Playground rollouts run in Python; write each finished episode to a local run directory and sync closed episodes to `rollouts/<env>/<policy>/<run_id>/` with rclone or s5cmd, or write directly with boto3. The [MuJoCo Rollout Dataset](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/mujoco-rollout-dataset) sample rolls out MuJoCo Playground policies, renders each episode, and writes MP4, `.npy` arrays and JSON under a rollout prefix with boto3 against `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. It serves presigned GETs for review and deletes by prefix; pass `VersionId` when deleting, since a plain delete only hides files on B2.

### NVIDIA Isaac Sim (asset region profiles)

Isaac Sim's `isaacsim.storage.native` extension documents an `asset_region_profiles` setting with an S3-compatible endpoint, bucket and region, applied in memory. Point the endpoint at `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, set the bucket and region, select the profile with `ISAACSIM_ASSET_REGION_PROFILE`, and supply credentials from the environment. Use it to load USD assets from `sim-assets/`. Isaac Lab and Isaac Lab Mimic write outputs to local paths; close those files and sync them with rclone.

### rclone

Use the [rclone B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/) to sync closed HDF5 files and run directories from workers or a shared staging disk. Give it a key restricted to `rollouts/`.

### Mounting assets in Kubernetes

Jobs that expect file paths can mount `sim-assets/` read-only with the Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI driver, as shown in the [B2 Mountpoint CSI sample](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-integration-mountpoint-csi). Do not mount the rollout prefix for in-place writes.

## Security

- Workers hold a writer key restricted to `rollouts/` and a read-only key for `sim-assets/`.
- Promotion and discarding use a separate operator key with `deleteFiles`; workers cannot delete.
- Isaac Sim settings files must not contain credentials; inject them at runtime.
- Record simulator version, asset version, seed and checkpoint in `config.json` so results are reproducible and asset licenses are traceable.

## References

- [MuJoCo Playground](https://playground.mujoco.org/)
- [MuJoCo Rollout Dataset architecture](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/mujoco-rollout-dataset/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Isaac Sim](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim) and its [storage settings](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/6.1.0/py/source/extensions/isaacsim.storage.native/docs/SETTINGS.html)
- [rclone B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [B2 Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive)

<!-- source: architectures/policy-training-registry/architecture.md -->

# Train and evaluate robot policies, checkpoint runs, and release models to the fleet

## Workload

Robot learning teams train visuomotor and vision-language-action (VLA) policies on multi-node GPU clusters that can be preempted. Checkpoints range from hundreds of MB to tens of GB and accumulate across runs. Candidates are evaluated in simulation benchmark suites. Promoted policies ship to robots and CI, and every release must trace back to its dataset version, code and eval results.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  DATA[(B2 datasets<br/>WebDataset shards / LeRobot v3)] -->|stream| TRAIN[Ray Train workers]
  BASE[(B2 hf-cache/<br/>base VLA weights)] --> TRAIN
  TRAIN -->|storage_path, endpoint_override| CK[(B2 training bucket<br/>checkpoints/run_id/)]
  TRAIN -->|run metadata| TRACK[MLflow / ClearML / W&B<br/>tracking server]
  TRACK -->|artifacts or references| CK
  CK --> EVAL[Sim benchmark suites]
  EVAL -->|videos, metrics| EV[(B2 training bucket<br/>eval/policy_version/suite/)]
  CK -->|promotion: server-side copy| REL[(B2 release bucket<br/>Object Lock<br/>models/policy/version/)]
  REL -->|release-signer key| SIGN[Fleet release service]
  SIGN -->|presigned GET per manifest file| FLEET[Robots and CI]
```

1. Trainers stream WebDataset shards or LeRobot v3 episodes from B2 (see [teleop-imitation-datasets](architectures/teleop-imitation-datasets/architecture.md)).
2. Ray Train writes checkpoints to `checkpoints/<run_id>/` and resumes from the latest after preemption. `CheckpointConfig(num_to_keep=K)` prunes older checkpoints; B2 lifecycle cannot keep "the last K".
3. MLflow or ClearML records runs and artifacts; W&B reference artifacts record dataset and checkpoint lineage without copying bytes.
4. Candidates run benchmark suites; eval videos and metrics go to `eval/<policy_version>/<suite>/`.
5. A promotion job server-side copies the chosen checkpoint to `models/<policy>/<version>/` in an Object Lock bucket with retention set, plus a manifest with checksums, dataset version, commit and eval summary.
6. A fleet release service holds the only read key on `models/<policy>/` and mints short-lived presigned GETs for each file in the release manifest. Robots and CI download with those URLs and verify checksums before loading; they hold no B2 keys.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Checkpoints | `<org>-robot-training/checkpoints/<run_id>/` | Purge hidden versions after a short window; delete abandoned runs ([lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | No | Resume state, pruned by the trainer |
| Eval artifacts | `<org>-robot-training/eval/<policy_version>/<suite>/` | Keep with the candidate's lifetime | No | Videos, metrics, rollouts |
| Tracking artifacts | `<org>-robot-training/mlflow/` or `clearml/` | Managed by the tracking server | No | Logged artifacts |
| Base model cache | `<org>-robot-training/hf-cache/` | Keep | No | Shared Hugging Face cache synced with [HF Cache Sync](https://github.com/backblaze-labs/hf-cache-sync) |
| Releases | `<org>-policy-releases/models/<policy>/<version>/` | Never overwritten | Yes, governance by default ([object-lock-evidence.json](examples/object-lock-evidence.json)) | Policies approved for the fleet |

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tracking metadata databases | MLflow, ClearML or W&B backends | Transactional run and registry state |
| Metrics time series | Tracking server | High-frequency small writes |
| Eval leaderboard | Database | Queries and updates |
| Dataloader cache and checkpoint staging | GPU-node NVMe | Low-latency local I/O |
| Distributed training rendezvous | Ray head / torch.distributed | Live coordination |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Ray Train, MLflow, ClearML, W&B, trainers |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB checkpoints |
| Server-side copy | Yes | Promote a checkpoint into the release bucket |
| Object Lock | Yes | Released policies |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Release downloads for robots and CI, minted by the fleet release service |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Trainers on `checkpoints/` and `eval/`; promotion alone writes `models/`; the fleet release service alone reads it |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Clean hidden versions and abandoned run prefixes |
| Event Notifications | Not used | Promotion is an explicit, reviewed step |
| Cloud Replication | Optional | DR copy of releases only; enable Object Lock on both buckets first |
| Overdrive vs local cache | Consider | [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) when many nodes read training data in parallel for sustained periods; NVMe staging for repeated epochs |

## Integration configuration

### Ray Train

Ray's persistent-storage guide has a Backblaze B2 section:

```python
from ray.train import RunConfig, CheckpointConfig
run_config = RunConfig(
    storage_path=f"s3://<org>-robot-training/checkpoints?endpoint_override=https://s3.{region}.backblazeb2.com",
    checkpoint_config=CheckpointConfig(num_to_keep=3),
)
```

Alternatively set the Arrow S3 environment variables and use a plain `s3://` path. The trainer key needs `deleteFiles` on `checkpoints/` because `num_to_keep` deletes older checkpoints. The [Ray Train/Tune checkpoints notebook](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/notebooks/tree/main/ray-train-tune-checkpoints) shows this against B2.

### MLflow

MLflow documents a native `b2://` artifact URI: `b2://<bucket>@s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<path>`. Use it as the tracking server's artifact root; keep the backend store (database) off B2.

### Weights & Biases (reference artifacts)

The W&B reference-artifact documentation names Backblaze B2 and uses `AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Reference artifacts record object URIs and checksums without uploading bytes, which suits multi-GB checkpoints and datasets that already live in B2.

### ClearML

ClearML's storage docs configure non-AWS endpoints in `sdk.aws.s3.credentials` with `host: "s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com:443"` and `secure: true`. The port is required.

## Security

- Training keys cover `checkpoints/` and `eval/` only and cannot write `models/`.
- The promotion job uses a short-lived key that can read the training bucket and write the release bucket with `writeFileRetentions` (see [examples](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys)).
- Robots and CI hold no B2 keys. The fleet release service holds a `release-signer` key restricted to `models/<policy>/` with `listFiles,readFiles`, authorizes each robot or CI job, and returns presigned GETs that expire shortly after the expected download window (at most 7 days for SigV4). Robots verify manifest checksums before loading a policy.
- Use governance-mode Object Lock by default; compliance mode cannot be shortened or removed.
- Tracking servers store B2 credentials; restrict who can change their artifact configuration.

## References

- [Ray Train persistent storage](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html)
- [MLflow artifact stores: Backblaze B2](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/#backblaze-b2)
- [W&B: track external files](https://docs.coreweave.com/guides/artifacts/track-external-files)
- [ClearML storage](https://clear.ml/docs/latest/docs/integrations/storage/)
- [WebDataset Streaming PyTorch Training](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/mapping-session-archive/architecture.md -->

# Archive LiDAR mapping sessions and publish site maps to robots

## Workload

Mobile robots map sites with LiDAR. Odometry and mapping jobs turn scans into poses, trajectories and point-cloud maps. Engineers re-map sites, update localization maps and debug drift, and every task needs the raw scans and all derived artifacts for a session kept together. Volumes reach GB to TB per site. Robots then need the current approved map for their site.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  BOT[Robot LiDAR] -->|presigned PUT / multipart| SCANS[(B2 mapping bucket<br/>scans/robot_id/session_id/)]
  SCANS --> ICP[KISS-ICP odometry job]
  ICP --> MAPS[(maps/session_id/map_*.ply<br/>trajectories/session_id/<br/>index.json)]
  SCANS --> O3D[Open3D job<br/>downsample, register, mesh]
  O3D --> JOBS[(jobs/id/<br/>artifacts + manifest)]
  MAPS -->|approval: server-side copy| SITE[(sitemaps/site/version/)]
  SITE -->|presigned GET| FLEET[Robots and RViz]
  SCANS -->|delete by VersionId| GONE[Rejected session]
```

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw scans | `<org>-robot-mapping/scans/<robot_id>/<session_id>/` | Keep while the site is active | No | Source LiDAR frames |
| Session maps | `<org>-robot-mapping/maps/<session_id>/` and `trajectories/<session_id>/` | Keep with the session | No | KISS-ICP poses, `.ply` maps, trajectories, `index.json` |
| Processing jobs | `<org>-robot-mapping/jobs/<id>/` | Hide after a window, then delete ([lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json)) | No | Open3D intermediates and previews |
| Site maps | `<org>-robot-mapping/sitemaps/<site>/<version>/` | Never overwritten | Optional | Approved maps served to robots |

`sitemaps/` is a separate prefix from the per-session `maps/` that KISS-ICP writes, so the approval key can be restricted to it.

On B2, `DeleteObjects` without a `VersionId` only hides each file; the bytes stay stored. To remove them, list the prefix with `ListObjectVersions` and delete by `VersionId` (needs `deleteFiles`), or rely on the `daysFromHidingToDeleting` rule in [lifecycle-scratch.json](examples/lifecycle-scratch.json), which purges hidden versions under `scans/`, `maps/` and `trajectories/` after a short grace period.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Live localization stack and map server | Robot | Real-time pose estimation |
| Spatial index database | PostGIS or similar | Queries by area and time |
| Odometry and meshing scratch | GPU or CPU node disk | Iterative in-memory work |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | PutObject, GetObject, ListObjectsV2, HeadObject, DeleteObjects in the samples |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | PUT for robot uploads, GET for maps and previews |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Large map snapshots and scan bundles |
| Server-side copy | Yes | Promote an approved session map to `sitemaps/` |
| Version-aware deletes | Yes | `ListObjectVersions` plus `DeleteObjects` by `VersionId` for rejected or re-mapped sessions |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire job intermediates; purge hidden versions under `scans/`, `maps/`, `trajectories/` |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Signing service, processing jobs and approval each have their own key |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Start odometry when a session's last scan lands |
| Object Lock, replication | Not used | Add only if maps are safety evidence |
| Overdrive | Not needed | Batch processing; site maps are small and cached on the robot |

## Integration configuration

### KISS-ICP

`kiss_icp_pipeline` reads scans from local paths and writes poses (`.npy`, KITTI and TUM text), the run config and a log to a local results directory. Copy a session's scans down, run the pipeline, then sync its results to `trajectories/<session_id>/` with rclone or s5cmd. The [KISS-ICP LiDAR Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/kiss-icp-lidar-archive) sample runs it on the backend and uses boto3 against `https://s3.<B2_REGION>.backblazeb2.com` (PutObject, GetObject, ListObjectsV2, HeadObject, DeleteObjects) with presigned GET and PUT, archiving scans, poses, `.ply` maps and trajectories per session.

### Open3D

Open3D reads and writes point clouds and meshes on local paths ([file IO](https://www.open3d.org/docs/release/tutorial/geometry/file_io.html)). Copy scans down, process them, and sync outputs to `jobs/<id>/` with rclone or s5cmd. The [Open3D Point Cloud Pipeline](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/open3d-point-cloud-pipeline) sample reads PLY, PCD, LAS and LAZ from `raw/`, writes downsampled, registered, meshed and rendered artifacts under `jobs/<id>/` with a JSON manifest, and serves presigned previews. Its endpoint is derived from `B2_REGION`. This architecture maps its `raw/` prefix to `scans/`.

## Security

- Robots upload scans and fetch site maps through presigned URLs minted by a site service; they hold no keys.
- Processing jobs read `scans/` and write only their own derived prefixes.
- Only the approval job writes `sitemaps/`, so robots never load an unapproved map.
- Deleting rejected sessions by `VersionId` needs `deleteFiles`; give it to a separate operator key per prefix, not to the signing service or processing jobs.
- Maps of customer sites can be confidential; scope signing and retention per customer or site, and use a bucket per customer when contracts require isolation.

## References

- [KISS-ICP](https://github.com/PRBonn/kiss-icp)
